Since $(\mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j}, \mathbf{v})$ is an orthonormal basis, the squared norm of the image-space gradient equals $\|\nabla_{\mathbf{o}} d(\mathbf{o}, \mathbf{v})\|^2 - \langle \nabla_{\mathbf{o}} d(\mathbf{o}, \mathbf{v}), \mathbf{v} \rangle^2$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in Source [S1] passages that since $(i, j, v)$ is an orthonormal basis, the squared norm of the image-space gradient $k∇d̃(x, y)k^2$ equals $⟨∇_o d(o, v), i⟩^2 + ⟨∇_o d(o, v), j⟩^2$. It further derives that $k∇_o d(o, v)k^2 = ⟨∇_o d(o, v), i⟩^2 + ⟨∇_o d(o, v), j⟩^2 + ⟨∇_o d(o, v), v⟩^2$. By rearranging this equation, the squared norm of the image-space gradient is shown to be $k∇_o d(o, v)k^2 - ⟨∇_o d(o, v), v⟩^2$. This matches the claim exactly.
